what: Manhattan Associates writes the software that runs warehouses: what to pick, where to put it, how to route the truck, and how to keep online and store inventory in one view.
customers: Large retailers, consumer goods makers and logistics operators with warehouses too complex to run on spreadsheets.
money: warehouse, order and transportation management sold by subscription
moat: Software embedded in how a warehouse physically operates. Replacing it means reconfiguring the building and retraining everyone in it, so customers almost never leave.
risks: 69 times earnings and 12 times sales, a price that assumes years of growth
Implementations are long, so a customer postponing a project delays revenue by quarters
Retail technology budgets tighten whenever consumer spending slows
opportunities: A 20.3% net margin and $380M of free cash flow on $1.2B of revenue, with $329M of cash and almost no debt
Revenue grew from $664M to $1.1B in four years as customers moved from licences to subscriptions
The subscription base is recurring revenue, which is worth more than the licence sales it replaced
watch: Remaining performance obligations, which show subscriptions already signed but not yet recognised.
